bottom_line: In patients with acute coronary syndromes with a planned invasive strategy, ticagrelor vs clopidogrel reduced the primary composite endpoint (hazard ratio 0.84, 95% CI 0.75–0.94).
implications: These results support that, in this planned invasive-strategy ACS population, ticagrelor was associated with a lower rate of the composite of cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, or stroke than clopidogrel (HR 0.84, 95% CI 0.75–0.94; p=0.0025). They do not support a difference in total major bleeding (HR 0.99, 95% CI 0.89–1.10; p=0.8803) or severe bleeding by the stated definition (HR 0.91, 95% CI 0.74–1.12; p=0.3785).

major_points.text: Primary endpoint occurred less often with ticagrelor than clopidogrel, with HR and p-value reported.
major_points.quote:
The primary composite endpoint
occurred in fewer patients in the ticagrelor group than in the clopidogrel group (569 [event rate at 360
days 9·0%] vs 668 [10·7%], hazard ratio 0·84, 95% CI 0·75–0·94; p=0·0025).

[11·5%], 0·99 [0·89–1·10]; p=0·8803)
